title: Embeddings onboarding: lightweight walkthrough tiles and progressive disclosure
creator: Maya Rodriguez
description: Create a compact, mobile-friendly onboarding flow for Embeddings + Rerank that fits into the Console quickstart area. Deliverables: a set of lightweight walkthrough tiles (3-5 steps) that progressively reveal advanced options (indexing settings, rerank threshold, similarity metric), a single-page printable cheatsheet for SRE/Platform teams, an accessible pipeline diagram (SVG) that explains ingest->embed->index->search->rerank->results, and three annotated sample outputs for docs and the in-console preview. The goal is to reduce first-run friction for engineers evaluating embeddings/rerank while surfacing cost and latency trade-offs without overwhelming novice users.
sample_outputs: Sample A - FAQ assistant: query 'How do returns work?' returns 3 ranked passages with similarity scores (0.92, 0.78, 0.61) and rerank highlights; include brief note on when to enable rerank for high-precision use cases.
Sample B - Support triage: top-1 match is high-sim (0.87) but rerank promotes a shorter canonical answer for latency-sensitive paths; show marked difference and token cost estimate.
Sample C - Semantic search fallback: low-sim query returns diverse matches and rerank suppressed due to low-confidence; show UI state 'Use broader context' and button to enable rerank anyway.
All samples include token cost estimate, representative sequence lengths, and a small table mapping settings -> expected latency/throughput.
acceptance_criteria: Three walkthrough tile variants reviewed and signed off by PM and ENG (A/B light, compact, and expanded).
Accessible pipeline SVG annotated with alt-text and suitable color contrast (WCAG AA).
Printable cheatsheet produced as single A4 PDF and uploaded to Drive with link in Console docs.
Sample outputs integrated into docs with captions, and linked GitHub PR includes in-console preview snapshots.
UX copy reviewed by Content and legal for claims about latency/cost.
design_notes: Prefer progressive disclosure: primary tile shows only 'Index your data' and 'Try with sample dataset'; 'Advanced' expands into indexing options (embedding model, chunk size, quantization hint).
Use micro-illustrations to communicate batching vs streaming trade-offs (one-liner caption).
Provide toggles in preview to flip between 'rerank on' and 'rerank off' and show delta in top-3 results and cost estimate inline.
Accessibility: ensure keyboard focus order on tiles, provide descriptive labels for similarity scores, avoid color as only signal for ranking badges.
Engineering constraint: keep tile payload < 20KB for initial render; avoid large embedded screenshots—use SVG and CSS where possible.
